newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds jump higher - OCT 29.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds jump higher - OCT 29.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities were sharply higher in line with Treasuries by late afternoon Tuesday.
Pass-throughs got their lift from a combination of soft

economic data earlier in the day, said traders. First, a moderate-than-expected 0.6 percent rise in the third-quarter employment cost index (ECI) initiated the rally. Then a drop in consumer confidence -- from a revised 111.8 in September to 106.2 in October -- fueled prices higher. "We've been hovering around the highs for he past couple of hours," said one trader. She said discount coupons have performed "quite nicely".
Late on Tuesday, pass-throughs were up 30/32 to over a full point higher in coupons of 7.0 percent or smaller, and were 6/32 to 28/32 higher in premium coupons.
Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent coupons were up 31/32 at 100-20/32, yielding 105 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable FNMAs were up 30/32 at 100-15/32, and FHLMCs were up 31/32 at 100-19/32.
The 10-year Treasury note climbed 1-1/4 point, with its yield sinking to 6.39 percent.
The 30-year Treasury yield fell to 6.68 percent, the lowest since 6.66 percent on April 4.
"I think the next stop on the yield basis is 6.66 (percent), said another mortgage-backed trader, adding "the fact that Halloween is this week ... there are forces beyond our control."
